stem_book: Why is BF₃ less acidic than BCl₃ despite fluorine being more electronegative than chlorine? (a) Because B–Cl bonds are stronger than B–F bonds (b) Due to the smaller atomic size of fluorine (c) Because fluorine can form strong pπ–pπ back bonds with boron (d) Because chlorine is more polarizable than fluorine
correct_answer: c Because fluorine can form strong pπ–pπ back bonds with boron
work: 2p(F)–2p(B) back-donation is efficient → B less electron-deficient in BF₃ → weaker Lewis acid
